findings.element: Tasks board, the card produced by the seam (.card[data-id="seam_*"]) on open-task
findings.problem: The one moment the whole suite exists to justify has no event. Sampled every frame across the crossing (70 frames, 27 tracked board elements), the entire visual result of a note becoming a task is the arriving card's own transform easing from translateY(-2px) scale(0.994) to identity over ~420ms. Nothing else on the board changes: no opacity, no background, no border-colour, no box-shadow, no ::before/::after, no lane flash, no head-count beat. After it settles the arrived card is byte-identical to its neighbour (same shadow string, same rgb(255,255,255), same rgb(17,17,17) border, outline none) and, because the crossing was pointer-initiated, :focus-visible is false so there is no ring either. It lands last in a lane of four cards that look exactly like it. A person who has just crossed from Notes has to read four titles to find the thing they sent. The behaviour gate proves a beat exists and is on the motion ladder; it cannot prove the beat reads, and a 2px rise and a 1.5px width change on a 256px card does not.
findings.fix: On open-task, set data-arrived on the landed card and hold it for the life of the existing 30-second undo window (clear it when the window closes or on first interaction with the card). In shell.css draw .card[data-arrived] with the indigo ring that already exists for [data-next] cards — box-shadow: rgba(79,70,229,0.32) 0 0 0 1px, rgba(17,17,17,0.02) 0 1px 1px 0, rgba(17,17,17,0.03) 0 2px 3px 0 — so no new colour is introduced. Raise the settle from translateY(-2px) scale(0.994) to translateY(-12px) scale(0.98) on the same enter duration already declared on the motion ladder, and scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) the card before the beat plays so it is on screen at every width.

findings.element: The capsule at 390x844 — the Notes / Tasks / Timeline tiles inside .dock
findings.problem: The architecture's claim is one rail rendered once, and on a phone the capsule and the dock are the same object. Measured at 390x844 with a touch pointer, the centre-x of the three product tiles is: in Notes 227 / 271 / 315 (pitch 44px, sitting in the right third); in Tasks 54 / 130 / 206 (pitch 76px, left); in Timeline 63 / 157 / 251 (pitch 94px, left). Every crossing moves the Notes tile 173px — 44% of the screen width — and changes the pitch. Tap Tasks at x=271 from Notes and you arrive in Tasks where Tasks is now at x=130 and x=271 is bare capsule between More (243) and Add task (295), so a second tap hits nothing or the wrong control. The one object that makes three products read as one application is measurably three objects, and it is the object under the thumb on every crossing.
findings.fix: Give the capsule a fixed three-slot spine: reserve the same left-hand grid for the Notes/Tasks/Timeline tiles in all three products at 44px pitch with the same first-tile centre-x (use Tasks' 54/130/206 as the ratified geometry, since Tasks already carries the fullest capsule), and lay the per-product tools (Notes' search/dictate/photo/save, Tasks' Add task, Timeline's nothing) into the slots to the right of the divider rather than pushing the spine across. The account tile already holds at 341-343 in all three; hold the spine the same way.

findings.element: Timeline, the moment editor opened from .b-grab — the WHAT IT IS and WHEN inputs
findings.problem: This is the only composition in the suite that does not hold, and no frame in the round shows it. The two inputs stretch to the full panel: 936px at 1280, 1096px at 1440, 1576px at 1920 — holding "Send the invitations" (20 characters) and "8 August 2026" (13 characters). Everything else in the panel — the -7/-1/+1/+7 steppers, the mono readout, WHAT GUESTS SEE, Close, Delete this moment — is hugged to x=213, so at 1920 the panel opens with an L-shaped void of roughly 1300x400px, plus a ~100px blank strip reserved at its head for an undo receipt that is not there at rest. The suite is disciplined about measure everywhere else (the gate even asserts Notes' index and paper share one). Here it simply gives up, on the surface where the person edits the object the whole Timeline direction is built on.
findings.fix: Cap both fields at a measure and left-align them with the rest of the panel: max-width: 34ch on the WHAT IT IS input and 20ch on the WHEN input, both with width:100% so they still shrink on a phone. Collapse the reserved receipt strip to height:0 when no undo is live rather than reserving it empty, and let it grow when the receipt appears.

findings.element: .railAvatar (rail foot) and .dockAvatar (dock) in Notes and Tasks at every desk width
findings.problem: The operator's monogram is rendered twice on the same screen: a ghost 32px OR at (34,900) on the rail foot and a filled-ink 34px OR at (907,883) in the dock at 1440 — 870px apart on the same eye-line, 1110px apart at 1920. Both are the same dead door: both aria-disabled, both opening the identical card "Not here yet." with the title "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet." Worse, the dock copy is filled ink at the same value as the "Add task" primary pill 15px to its left, so the two read as one two-part control and the second loudest object in the dock is a door that does not open. Timeline has neither dock nor second copy, so the suite is also inconsistent about where identity lives. Two identical avatars, one of them shouting, is the kind of thing a discerning stranger reads as a bug before they read it as a design.
findings.fix: Drop .dockAvatar from the desk dock in both Notes and Tasks (keep it on the phone capsule, where the rail does not exist and it is the only copy) and keep the rail-foot .railAvatar as the single home for identity in all three products. If a presence in the dock is wanted, demote it to the rail's ghost treatment — 1px rgba(17,17,17,0.28) ring on white, ink-2 initials — so no closed door carries the same ink value as the product's primary act.

findings.element: Timeline at 390x844 — the capsule tile aria-label="More" and the head's "···" aria-label="More"; and the missing More on the Notes phone
findings.problem: On the Timeline phone two controls are visible at once whose accessible name is exactly "More": the capsule grid tile, 44x44 at (297,783), which is the unbuilt honest door, and a "···" button, 39x44 at (160,140), which opens the real menu carrying Preview and the link. Same word, two destinations, one 390px screen — a screen-reader user hears "More button" twice with no way to tell which is the dead one. Separately, on the Notes phone the honest "More" door measures 0x0 (its .railUtil copy is collapsed with the rail and the Notes capsule carries no More tile), while Tasks keeps its at (243,783) and Timeline at (297,783). The doors are meant to be present and reachable; in one product at one width one of them simply is not there.
findings.fix: Rename the Timeline head's "···" to aria-label="Timeline options", matching the "Notes options" grammar already used in the Notes head, and leave "More" to the capsule door alone. In the Notes phone capsule, add the same 44x44 More tile Tasks and Timeline carry, placed in the slot immediately left of the account tile, so the four honest doors are present in all three products at all widths.

biggestWin: The Timeline horizon screen. "79" set enormous in Geist 400 with "days" whispered at its foot, "Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day" beside it, and "TODAY IS 16 JULY" sitting under a single indigo hairline — a whole season of work made legible in one glance, with no chart, no colour coding and no chrome. It is the one screen here that would sit unembarrassed next to Linear or Stripe, and it does the emotional work the product promises: a person who runs weddings for a living looks at it and knows, in one beat, exactly how much room she has left. The writing carries the same win — "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit." and "Nothing is decided until you say so, and every decision can be put back." are better sentences than most funded products ever ship, and they remove the exact fear each gesture creates.
